快速 FLF 循环工作流程 — MiniMax H3

速度优化的第一帧和最后一帧工作流程迷你最大H3，专为生成无缝循环视频剪辑而构建 - 为其提供与第一帧和最后一帧相同的图像，它会渲染一个干净地循环回到开头的剪辑。非常适合 VJ 循环、背景视觉效果、动作设计以及任何其他需要重复运行且没有可见接缝的内容。

此版本在标准 H3 FLF 设置之上添加了速度堆栈：圣人注意(KJ节点) +易缓存，默认情况下步数从 20 减少到 15。每个节点的所有内容都是可绕过的，因此您可以自己对速度和质量进行 A/B 测试。

测试设置

测试于RTX 5080 (16GB VRAM) 和 64GB 系统 RAM。以下所有基准数据均来自该机器 - 将它们视为参考点，而不是保证。如果您运行不同的 GPU 或 RAM 量，您的时间会有所不同，有时会很明显：​​较少的 VRAM 会将更多模型推向卸载（较慢），较少的系统 RAM 可能会成为该工作流程所依赖的动态 VRAM 分段的瓶颈，而较旧的 GPU 架构将无法从 Sage Attention 的融合内核中获得相同的好处。

应该在哪里运行：任何具有 16GB+ VRAM 的 RTX 40 系列或 50 系列（Ada/Blackwell）卡都应该可以轻松处理 1.0 兆像素。 30 系列和更旧的卡仍然可以工作，但 Sage Attention 会回退到旧内核，而没有相同的加速 - 预计渲染时间会明显更长。在 ~12GB VRAM 下，坚持更接近 0.4 兆像素的预览分辨率。



关于 337 与 234 差距的注释：启动 ComfyUI（或加载不同模型后）后的第一代通常需要更长的时间，因为模型仍在暂存到 VRAM 中。一旦所有内容都加载完毕，在相同模型上进行第二次连续渲染将会明显更快 - 这就是 234s 数字的来源。仅当您立即排队另一代，而不切换模型或执行任何其他强制重新加载的操作时，这才成立。将您自己的数字与上面的数字进行比较时请记住这一点。

关于 EasyCache 质量：在默认阈值下，EasyCache 通过重用几乎相同的中间结果来跳过大约一半的采样步骤。这是一个很大的加速，但不是免费的——抽象/几何循环很好地隐藏了它，细节较多或字符内容则不然。推荐：打开 EasyCache 进行预览和迭代，绕过（或将阈值降低到 ~0.1）进行最终渲染。

世代示例

包括两个示例输出，均使用与工作流程捆绑在一起的眼镜蛇参考图像（匹配提示在第一帧/最后一帧调节中预加载）：

  • 1.0兆像素渲染

  • 0.4兆像素渲染

将眼镜蛇图像加载到第一帧和最后一帧 LoadImage 节点中以重现示例，或者交换您自己的匹配第一帧/最后一帧对。

Fast FLF Loop Workflow — MiniMax H3

A speed-optimized First & Last Frame workflow forMiniMax H3, built for generating seamless looping video clips — feed it the same image as both the first and last frame and it renders a clip that loops cleanly back to its start. Ideal for VJ loops, background visuals, motion design, and anything else that needs to run on repeat without a visible seam.

This version adds a speed stack on top of the standard H3 FLF setup:Sage Attention(KJNodes) +EasyCache, with steps reduced from 20 to 15 by default. Everything is bypassable per-node so you can A/B test speed against quality yourself.

Tested setup

Tested on anRTX 5080 (16GB VRAM) with 64GB system RAM. All benchmark numbers below come from that machine — treat them as a reference point, not a guarantee. If you're running a different GPU or amount of RAM, your times will vary, sometimes significantly: less VRAM will push more of the model into offloading (slower), less system RAM can bottleneck the dynamic VRAM staging this workflow relies on, and older GPU architectures won't get the same benefit from Sage Attention's fused kernels.

Where this should run:any RTX 40-series or 50-series (Ada/Blackwell) card with 16GB+ VRAM should comfortably handle this at 1.0 megapixel. 30-series and older cards will still work, but Sage Attention falls back to older kernels without the same speedup — expect noticeably longer render times. Under ~12GB VRAM, stick closer to the 0.4 megapixel preview resolution.



A note on that 337s vs 234s gap:your first generation after starting ComfyUI (or after loading a different model) will usually take longer, since models are still being staged into VRAM. Once everything's loaded, a second render back-to-back on the same models will be noticeably faster — that's where the 234s number comes from. This only holds if you queue another generation right after, without switching models or doing anything else that forces a reload in between. Keep that in mind when comparing your own numbers to the ones above.

On EasyCache quality:at the default threshold, EasyCache skips roughly half the sampling steps by reusing near-identical intermediate results. That's a big speedup but not free — abstract/geometric loops hide it well, detail-heavy or character content less so. Recommended: EasyCache on for previews and iteration, bypassed (or threshold lowered to ~0.1) for final renders.

Example generations

Two sample outputs included, both using the cobra reference image bundled with the workflow (matching prompt is preloaded in the first/last frame conditioning):

  • 1.0 megapixelrender

  • 0.4 megapixelrender

Load the cobra image into both the first-frame and last-frame LoadImage nodes to reproduce the examples, or swap in your own matching first/last frame pair.
